defects: Glowing trail is visibly beaded: you can count the separate sample points along the path in 'Every switchback.' and on the end card instead of seeing one continuous stroke, and it gets worse at the leading edge (pairs row 2)
The 'Every' transition is a flat hard-edged panel slide with no motion blur and no easing on the edge. The vertical seam reads like a compositing split, not a designed wipe
'Works offline.' shot: the 'Ridge Loop' header is cut off at the top of the frame and the bar sits flush against the left edge; it looks like an accidental crop
Phone mockup in the 3D shot is too small and too soft to read. The UI text turns to mush and the flat screen sits on the terrain with no contact shadow or reflection

Near-static holds (per-second change about 8 at 4s and 13s) where the camera drift is so slight it reads as a frozen frame, not a deliberate hold ('0 BARS NEEDED' barely changes between the two frames of its pair)
Terrain is a low-frequency displaced mesh with cloth-like shading. It has no micro detail, no scale cues and only soft fog, so it feels like a default procedural look
Uniform heavy grain over flat dark areas looks like it was added to hide banding, not graded in
gaps: Choreography: almost all of it is slow push-ins, one slide and a trail draw-on. There are no motivated camera moves connecting map to terrain to type, no match-cuts between the contour map and the 3D landscape (the obvious idea), and no secondary or overlapping animation to give weight

Finish: a top studio would render the trail as a continuous, sub-frame-sampled glowing stroke with proper bloom falloff, give the terrain real material and lighting detail, and stage the device as a hero object, not a flat card stuck in a hill

Sound: the spectrogram shows mostly broadband noise risers and whooshes over a thin, static low bed with little harmonic movement. Tonal content only really appears in the final resolve around 12.6s. Hits line up with some cuts, but there is no layered sound design (UI ticks, foley, a terrain texture) and no real musical arc
